business_scope.primary_industry_name: Medical Device FDA 510(k) Filing and European CE Mark Compliance

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: New Zealand (national company registry jurisdiction; no sub-state company registers)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (unitary; Companies Act 1993 is the primary corporations statute, supplemented by the AML/CFT Act 2009 and subordinate regulations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CPTPP - Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (in force for NZ since 30 December 2018; investment chapter with ISDS)
New Zealand-China Free Trade Agreement (2008) and Investment Protocol upgrade (in force 2020)
New Zealand-Hong Kong, China Closer Economic Partnership Agreement / CEP (in force 1 January 2011)
New Zealand-European Union Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 May 2024; applicable to digital trade and MedTech regulatory cooperation)
ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement / AANZFTA (2010; investment chapter)
Australia-New Zealand Closer Economic Relations Agreement / ANZCERTA (1983; investment facilitation)
Double Taxation Agreements with major MedTech source markets, including US (1982), UK (1983), Australia (2009), Singapore (2009) and China (as amended 2019)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand): s. 10 (formation of company), s. 12 (issue of certificate of incorporation), s. 16 (constitution may be filed), ss. 47-49 (registered office), ss. 87-89 (share allotment and share register), s. 128 (no minimum capital requirement), ss. 151-159 (directors), ss. 189-190 (registered office requirements); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (only if public offer); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT obligations for designated financial services).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), part of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (online electronic form NZ1) filed via the Companies Office portal with integrated RealMe identity verification; upon approval the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Companies Act 1993; a company may be incorporated with issued shares of zero par value and no paid-up capital. No escrow account or capital deposit is required at incorporation. Directors must, however, ensure solvency and that the company will be able to meet its obligations as they fall due.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — RESOLVED, as recorded on this ___ day of ____________ 20___, by the initial director(s) of [COMPANY NAME] (the Company), as follows: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: That the issue and allotment of ______ ordinary shares, par value NZD 0.00 per share, to the subscriber named in the application for incorporation be and is hereby approved; the directors shall record the allotment in the share register in accordance with ss. 87-89 of the Companies Act 1993; the initial shareholding shall be credited as fully subscribed and any consideration, being NIL or NZD ____, shall be recorded without requiring an escrow arrangement given the absence of any statutory minimum paid-up capital. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed and adopted at [STREET ADDRESS, TOWN/CITY, POSTCODE] in New Zealand, and that the Registrar of Companies be notified of such office in accordance with s. 12 and ss. 189-190 of the Companies Act 1993; the registered office shall be open to the public during ordinary business hours and all statutory records shall be maintained at such address or at the company's recorded record address. (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as sole/executive director of the Company, and [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as company secretary (if applicable), each to serve subject to the Companies Act 1993 and any constitution adopted by the Company; the directors are hereby severally and jointly authorized to open and operate corporate bank accounts, execute service agreements, appoint the registered agent and tax advisors, and take all ancillary actions to give effect to this resolution. PASSED UNANIMOUSLY AND DECLARED EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — online Business Name / Company Name search and registration portal (via RealMe login)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Companies Office online name search tool and run an availability query for the proposed company name. If the name is available, proceed with reservation as part of the incorporation application; if the name is not available, select a distinguishable alternative. Names containing restricted words (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Insurance') require approval from the Financial Markets Authority or other regulator; such consent must be uploaded at filing.
required_dossiers: Name clearance/consent letter (if restricted word used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a direction to change the name or rejects the name, the applicant may submit a revised name through the same portal or file a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 1993 s. 25; any mistaken refusal may be cured by re-submission with supporting trade-mark or common-law usage evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Company Constitution (Optional but Recommended)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders and initial director(s); not filed with the Companies Office unless voluntarily registered
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written constitution in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 s. 16 and the First Schedule default rules. If the company does not adopt a constitution, the statutory default rules in the Companies Act 1993 will govern. For the International Company structure, adopt a bespoke constitution providing for no par value shares, unlimited corporate capacity, delegated board authority, and indemnification of directors to the fullest extent permitted by law. The constitution must be signed by all shareholders before or at incorporation and may be delivered to the Companies Office for registry record if desired.
required_dossiers: Board consent to adopt constitution (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defective provision is identified, the constitution may be amended by special resolution under s. 32 of the Companies Act 1993; re-executed pages are to be filed with the Companies Register if the constitution was registered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Electronic Application for Incorporation (Form NZ1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies) — online filing through the Companies Register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation application (electronic NZ1) through the Companies Office website using RealMe authenticated credentials. Input the proposed company name, registered office address, directors' full legal names, birth dates, addresses, and consent to act, shareholder details and share allocation, and any constitution adoption. Confirm that the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand (not a postal box). Electronically sign the declaration of compliance and submit the prescribed fee of NZD 105.50 (approximately USD 64) by credit card or online banking.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of a Company (NZ1 online form)
Consent to act of each director and each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended by the Registrar due to incomplete or inconsistent data, the applicant must correct the flagged fields and resubmit within the Registrar's given timeframe; a formal notice of deficiency may be cured by filing an amendment via the portal. If the Registrar declines incorporation, the applicant may apply for judicial review or re-present corrected documents; in practice, the majority of queries are administrative and cured within 1-2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies; New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation electronically, and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) is automatically allocated by the NZBN register through the Companies Office system. Verify that the certificate records the correct company number, the company name, the date of incorporation, and confirmation that the company is a limited liability company he reby authorized to commence business.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains any clerical error in company name or date, the director must immediately notify the Registrar in writing via the Companies Register amendment function; rectification is completed under the Registrar's correction powers without court order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: IRD Number Registration and Tax Account Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand; optional application via myIR or through the Companies Office data transfer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NZBN number to apply for an Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number and income tax registration. Newly incorporated companies are generally automatically issued an IRD number after registration with the Companies Office, but confirmation must be obtained in myIR. Register for resident withholding tax and, if annual revenue exceeds NZD 60,000, GST. For a non-resident owned International Company electing tax-exempt treatment, file the appropriate non-resident declaration and claim any applicable double tax agreement or exemption certificate through the IRD.
required_dossiers: Estimated turnover figures for GST registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is not auto-issued within 10 business days, file a paper IRD application (IR596) with supporting identification; any incorrect tax status may be rectified by filing a notice of assessment adjustment in myIR within the statutory response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Director Address Filing Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register maintenance portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office address and directors' residential addresses are accurately recorded in the Companies Register. Any change of registered office, directors, or director addresses must be filed online within 20 working days of the change pursuant to s. 190 of the Companies Act 1993. The registered agent (if any) must hold a New Zealand physical address and be recorded as the communication address for the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Registered office address (physical New Zealand address)
Consent to act for any newly appointed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Register flags a non-compliant registered office (e.g., postal box only), the company must file an online address update with a compliant street address; failure to maintain a registered office exposes the company to removal from the Register under s. 314, which can be cured by an application for restoration under s. 329.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and AML/KYC Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand banks (e.g., the major trading banks); Financial Markets Authority and Internal Affairs AML/CFT supervisors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account by presenting the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, constitution, director/shareholder due diligence information, and a board resolution approving bank signatories. The bank will perform customer due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2009. For this MedTech consulting entity, ensure the bank's risk classification is updated to reflect the Low_Risk_Standard tier for professional consulting fees receivable by bank wire and credit card.
required_dossiers: Passport and proof of address for all signatories and ultimate beneficial owners
Business plan and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence or rejects the application, provide additional evidence of the non-physical consulting business model (e.g., client contracts, regulatory consultancy scope) and the absence of high-risk product flow; the company may also approach the Banking Ombudsman Scheme if a denial is procedurally improper.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial establishment is proposed under ISIC 7490 (professional, scientific and technical regulatory consulting). If the company later acquires a physical office, the relevant authority is the applicable Territorial Authority (City/District Council) under the Building Act 2004 and the local District Plan; any manufacturing or laboratory activity would require a resource consent from the local council and occupational licensing through WorkSafe New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the company does not require an industrial operating/manufacturing permit for FDA 510(k) filing and European CE Mark regulatory compliance consulting services. A standard business premises occupancy permit (building warrant of fitness) is only required where a physical office is leased.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand (central regulator), in coordination with regional councils under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the Natural and Built Environment Act 2023
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Registration only; no full EIA required. Office-based regulatory consulting activities fall outside the specified Schedule of activities and do not trigger a formal Environmental Impact Assessment. No discharge of contaminants, no wastewater, no significant VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste generation occurs in the business model.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A — the business does not operate a point source discharge. Should the company ever establish laboratory or light-assembly premises, it must comply with: (a) regional council Trade Waste Bylaws for any aqueous effluent; (b) Ministry for the Environment National Environmental Standards on air quality limiting VOCs; (c) EPA Hazardous Substances (Hazardous Property) regulations for storage of reagents; and (d) the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for correct disposal of any electronic or chemical waste. As a consulting office, all waste must be disposed through licensed municipal waste contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the proposed office premises only: (1) Fire Safety — a Fire Evacuation Scheme and/or building fire compliance certificate under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) Act 2017 and the Building Act 2004; where the leased building has a compliance schedule, the tenant must comply with the Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) regime and annual building inspections; (2) Structural — the council issue a Certificate of Title / Code Compliance Certificate confirming the premises meet the structural load requirements of the Building Code; (3) Workplace — a general health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (WorkSafe NZ), including a documented worker engagement plan, hazard register, and first-aid provisions; and (4) Civil defense — the premises must display the local council civil defence emergency coordination information and participate in an evacuation drill if required by the FENZ evacuation scheme.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tauhake) of New Zealand; operational portal: myIR at www.ird.govt.nz; customs administration for export documentation: New Zealand Customs Service (Te Mana Ārai o Aotearoa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-incorporated International Company (CK_IC) seeking registration in New Zealand: (1) Determine whether the entity has a sufficient nexus with New Zealand, such as carrying on a taxable activity, having a permanent establishment, supplying goods or services in New Zealand, or incurring employer obligations; (2) Apply for an IRD number using the appropriate registration pathway, normally through the myIR portal or the IR742 application for non-resident companies where the entity is not incorporated under the Companies Act 1993; if the entity establishes a New Zealand branch, register the overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office and then apply for the IRD number; (3) If the entity makes or intends to make taxable supplies in New Zealand, register for GST through myIR using the IR303 form when total taxable supplies in any 12-month period is NZD 60,000 or more, or when voluntarily registering as a non-resident supplier of remote services; (4) Present the IRD number certificate, certificate of incorporation, and proof of director identity to the New Zealand bank when opening an account supporting bank wire and credit card payment rails; (5) Maintain a New Zealand address for service and appoint a local agent when required; (6) File GST returns in the assigned filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly) and maintain the statutory export evidence files for any zero-rated supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. Applicable statutory mechanisms include: (a) look-through company (LTC) election under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 for closely held New Zealand companies, not available to a non-resident international company structure; (b) controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution and branch-equivalent elections under Subparts CQ and EX for New Zealand residents with interests in foreign companies; (c) GST grouping election under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1986; (d) hybrid mismatch neutralisation rules under Subpart FH and Subpart GB intended to prevent double non-taxation through entity/hybrid mismatches; (e) unilateral tax exemption or double tax agreement relief for offshore sourced income of non-resident companies where the entity does not have a New Zealand permanent establishment; (f) consumption tax registration elections for non-resident suppliers under the remote services regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (compulsory registration is triggered when total taxable supplies in any 12-month period exceed NZD 60,000; non-resident suppliers of remote services are subject to the same threshold and, where applicable, must register and charge GST on supplies to New Zealand consumers, with reverse-charge or platform-collection obligations for certain B2B and B2C digital supplies)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or invoice-level pre-approval API regime exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates under the New Zealand e-Invoice framework using the Peppol BIS 3.0 standard, with mandatory adoption only for government-agency receivables through accredited Peppol access points. GST returns (IR303) are filed electronically via myIR or certified third-party software. There is no national two-way API clearance obligation for commercial invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% GST is available where the supplier can substantiate the supply under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1986. For goods: the supplier must export the goods outside New Zealand within 28 days of supply (or within an approved longer period) and retain transport documentation. For services, including medical device FDA 510(k) and CE Mark regulatory consulting: the supply must be supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, or the services must relate to intellectual property, know-how, or data supplied to a non-resident recipient that is not registered and not liable to be registered for GST in New Zealand, and the supply must not be directly connected with land or goods situated in New Zealand. Additional eligibility criteria include: the services benefit a taxable activity carried on outside New Zealand by the recipient; the recipient provides a valid overseas business address; the contract contains a zero-rating representation clause; and the supplier holds contemporaneous evidence of payment in foreign currency and the professional nature of the regulatory consulting engagement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export entry lodged with the New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/telex confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit zero-rated export supplies and retrospectively claw back any GST refunded where the documentary evidence is insufficient, the goods are not exported within the statutory time frame, or the services are found to be supplied to or consumed by a person in New Zealand. Reassessments may extend up to four years, and longer where evasion is established. Use-of-money interest runs from the original due date. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply at tiered rates: 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, and up to 100% for evasion or a similar act, while dishonest or fraudulent behaviour may attract additional monetary penalties. Criminal conviction for knowingly zero-rating taxable supplies without lawful entitlement can result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine not exceeding NZD 50,000. The GST-registered supplier remains jointly and severally liable for the clawback and penalties irrespective of any recovery action taken against the overseas recipient.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) is the central bank and sole monetary authority in New Zealand; it exercises prudential regulation over all registered banks and administers the International Transaction Reporting System (ITRS). The Financial Markets Authority (FMA) supervises AML/CFT compliance for non-bank financial institutions and financial advisers, while the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) under Land Information New Zealand screens only 'sensitive' land or significant business-asset acquisitions, which are not engaged for an advisory-only International Company. There is no separate foreign-exchange control authority; exchange controls were abolished in 1984.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The NZD is fully convertible on both current and capital account for residents and non-residents. There are no restrictions on the purchase, sale, or transfer of foreign currency, no approval requirements for dividends, management fees, royalties, loan repayments, or sale proceeds, and no differentiated treatment for offshore or tax-exempt entities. The only frictions are (i) the bank's AML/CFT due diligence before executing large transfers, (ii) statistical reporting of international transactions via the bank's International Funds Transfer Instruction (IFTI) when the transaction is over NZD 10,000, and (iii) non-resident withholding tax on any NZ-source dividends or interest. MedTech consulting fees earned from foreign clients are not NZ-source income and can be accumulated offshore or repatriated freely.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand does not impose any export-proceeds surrender obligation. Since the deregulation of the financial system in 1984, no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation quota applies to export receipts or service fees. An exporting or consulting company may keep foreign currency proceeds in overseas accounts, convert at a time of its choosing, or settle forward contracts without regulatory consent. The sole administrative duties are that the bank retain underlying invoices/contracts for at least 7 years, and that any individual cross-border transfer exceeding NZD 10,000 be recorded in the RBNZ's IFTI reporting return.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for inbound multi-currency collection (USD/EUR/GBP) and outbound disbursements, but Low for primary settlement. Global EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Tazapay are not registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and may not accept NZD deposits from the public; they operate under the Financial Service Providers Act 2008 (FSPR registration) or hold an Australian AFSL/ACL and provide local-account virtual numbers through partner banks. Legally, the IC remains the sole reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009 for its own transactions even where the EMI provides the rail, and the EMI is entitled to perform its own KYC, sanctions screening, and transaction monitoring at account-opening. For a Low-Risk Advisory entity, an EMI is viable as a secondary collection-and-disbursement channel, but the tier-1 NZ bank must remain the treasury anchor to preserve clean SWIFT BIC/IBAN routing and creditworthiness.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: None of the four major banks require physical presence of directors at account opening; remote onboarding with a video interview and certified corporate documents is standard for low-risk, non-resident consulting entities. The mandated evidence set includes: certificate of incorporation (for a Cook Islands International Company (IC) a certificate of good standing from the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission), a constitution/company resolution, register of directors and ultimate beneficial owners, notarized passport copies apostilled in the home jurisdiction, an NZD-denominated registered office address, and a New Zealand business number (NZBN) and IRD number or an explicit signed declaration of non-residence for New Zealand tax purposes. Kiwibank may request the physical signature of the account signatory if no NZBN exists; the majors accept a notarized signature page via courier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity – IC shares held by nominee, trust, or bearer instruments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute a full register of members and UBO declarations; provide the deed of trust or nominee agreement, notarized passports of all natural persons behind the trust, a certificate of good standing from the IC registry, and a bank-compliant UBO coverage schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected 'pass-through' transaction pattern – frequent receipts from MedTech clients followed by immediate outbound payments to FDA/CE consultants with minimal margin retained.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver signed engagement letters and sub-consultancy agreements, itemized invoices and timesheets demonstrating service delivery, a gross-margin analysis, FDA/Notified Body correspondence evidencing the IC's substantive role, and QBO/Xero financial reports showing controlled cash conversion cycles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt / offshore classification (Tax_Exempt_Zone) raising economic-substance red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a substance memorandum demonstrating decision-making, staff, and service-execution locations; a copy of the IC's tax-exemption certificate; IRD non-residence declaration; and detailed project files for each FDA 510(k) or CE Mark client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound credit-card receipts with overseas-issued cards and no physical New Zealand presence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implement a compliant merchant facility with transparent descriptor 'MedTech Regulatory Consulting'; maintain signed client contracts, customer identification records for the Consultation Services Agreement, chargeback procedures, and reconciliation reports satisfying the low-risk standard.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing is a SWIFT MT103 from the parent company's bank to the IC's operating account at the NZ tier-1 bank. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must cite 'Capital contribution to International Company [IC registration number]' with purpose code 'EQ – Equity Capital' in the bank's IFTI classification so the RBNZ can classify the flow without further inquiry. Supporting documents must be pre-submitted before the wire: (i) board resolution of the IC approving the equity subscription, (ii) certificate of good standing of the IC, (iii) passport copies of the contributing beneficial owner, and (iv) source-of-funds statements from the remitting bank. If the liquidity event is a shareholder loan, use purpose code 'LO – Intercompany Loan' and provide a signed loan agreement with an interest-rate schedule and an intercompany balance sheet. No Overseas Investment Office consent is required for a service company with no sensitive land and business assets below NZD 100 million; the only statutory step is the bank's statistical IFTI return.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service-related disbursements (payments to FDA consultants, EU Notified Bodies, legal counsel, and subcontractors), the standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) because it provides a complete audit trail and is accepted by all financial institutions globally. A commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700) is permissible for substantial project-specific purchases but is uncommon for consulting services; a standby LC is preferable for securing performance obligations. Inbound client origination fees from medical-device sponsors are collected by direct card acquiring through the tier-1 bank's merchant facility (Visa/Mastercard clearing settlement into the IC's operational account T+1) or by SWIFT/ACH/SEPA transfer converted into NZD using a spot contract. Every outbound disbursement exceeding NZD 10,000 must be supported by an underlying engagement contract, a purchase order (if applicable), and an itemized invoice to satisfy both the bank's AML/CFT obligations and New Zealand's record-keeping requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla NZD/USD and NZD/EUR outright forwards with NZ-registered banks (FXA flexi-forwards available)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/EUR where the IC hedges foreign-currency receivables with offshore counterparties
Vanilla FX options (purchases of currency calls/puts) for premium-limited upside protection
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (XCCY) to align non-NZD assets and liabilities, permitted for wholesale clients under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 derivatives regime
FX swap rollovers (spot/forward combinations) used to manage short-term NZD liquidity without executing a second physical transfer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form AR) — Companies Act 1993, s.214
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 working days after the annual return date (usually the anniversary of incorporation; may be aligned to the company’s balance date by filing notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is an offence; each director is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding NZ$10,000. If annual returns are missed for 3 consecutive years, the Registrar may send notice of proposed removal and strike the company off the Companies Register if no objection is raised within 20 working days.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Report (only if audit threshold is met or shareholder-required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office; shareholders where the company is exempt from public filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be completed within 5 months of balance date; if non-exempt, file them with the Companies Office together with the annual return (within 28 working days after the annual return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may incur fines up to NZ$10,000 for failing to prepare or file required statements; continued non-compliance may trigger removal from the Companies Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit applies only where the company is 'large' (total assets exceeding NZ$30 million or total revenue exceeding NZ$15 million), is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, or shareholders holding 5% of voting rights require an audit. A private International Company conducting only non-resident consulting activity is ordinarily below these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: If financial statements are required, they must comply with NZ IFRS as adopted by the External Reporting Board; smaller non-reporting companies may use the XRB A1 simplified reporting standard. Where no public filing is required, internal management accounts may be prepared in accordance with a consistently applied GAAP selected by the board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand company law does not require a separate UBO annual filing; the annual return and the register of members provide the official annual confirmation of shareholding. Every share transfer during the year must be approved by the board, recorded in the Register of Members, and reflected in the next annual return. AML/CFT-regulated service providers are separately obliged to maintain current beneficial-ownership records on a risk-based customer relationship basis.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150–US$600 per annum for New Zealand registered office/agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000–US$10,000 per annum for a statutory audit of a small consulting entity, if triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (New Zealand resident corporate tax rate); nil effective rate on foreign-sourced income of a qualifying non-resident International Company in the tax-exempt zone.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Company tax exemption permits 0% taxation on non-New Zealand-sourced FDA 510(k) and CE Mark regulatory consulting fees, provided the company is not managed and controlled in New Zealand and has no New Zealand permanent establishment. New Zealand-source business income would be subject to 28% corporate tax. No separate capital gains tax applies to asset sales outside New Zealand. Preferential treatment also includes non-resident withholding tax relief under applicable double taxation agreements and the Approved Issuer Levy at 2% for certain eligible interest arrangements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed through Inland Revenue MyIR portal at www.ird.govt.nz or approved tax software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (companies with New Zealand taxable income may also have provisional tax instalment obligations three times a year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the income year. With a registered tax agent, the filing extension may allow lodgement by 31 March of the following income year. For non-standard balance dates, the return is due by the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IRD number, legal name, registered office address and industry classification code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the New Zealand IRD number issued to the International Company. A non-resident International Company deriving no New Zealand-source income and with no permanent establishment in New Zealand is not ordinarily required to file an IR4; if filing, explicitly identify as a non-resident company and confirm absence of a New Zealand PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from carrying on business in New Zealand, expressed in NZD.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only fees for FDA 510(k) and CE Mark regulatory consulting services that are attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment. Foreign-sourced consulting fees are excluded under the International Company tax exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total allowable deductions and expenses directly attributable to reportable New Zealand-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenditures incurred in producing New Zealand-source revenue. General offshore head-office costs and global marketing costs require transfer pricing allocation; no apportionment of exempt foreign-source income is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or net loss before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply correct apportionment for cross-border consulting projects. Losses attributable to exempt foreign activity cannot reduce New Zealand taxable income; any deductible tax loss carryforward is capped at five income years for tax-exempt-zone International Companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 28% corporate rate to New Zealand-source taxable income. If the company is fully exempt on foreign income and has no New Zealand taxable income, enter nil and attach an explanatory schedule of residency and tax exemption status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for resident withholding tax, imputation credits and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits for New Zealand RWT on interest or dividends and any New Zealand provisional tax payments. A non-resident may also attach a statement of foreign tax credits where treaty relief has been granted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 include an initial NZD 250 penalty, with further penalty exposure if the return remains overdue for more than 30 days. Late payment penalties begin at 1% of the unpaid tax and are followed by 4% additional penalties on each subsequent six-month anniversary of the due date. Use-of-money interest is also charged daily on unpaid tax. Deliberate evasion carries a 150% shortfall penalty and criminal prosecution exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory New Zealand non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on non-imputed dividends to non-residents; 15% NRWT for fully imputed dividends; nil for dividends paid from a qualifying International Company out of exempt foreign-sourced income with no New Zealand source connection.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA) reduced rate, the non-resident recipient must submit Inland Revenue form IR822 before payment and provide a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction tax authority. The form must establish beneficial ownership of the income and residency for treaty purposes. If NRWT is over-withheld, the recipient may file an annual tax return to obtain a refund. For a tax-exempt International Company, treaty relief is unnecessary where the income lacks New Zealand source and no NRWT applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: New Zealand statutory NRWT on interest and royalties paid to non-residents is 15% for each category. Under many NZ DTAs, the rates are commonly reduced to 10% for interest and 5% for royalties where the recipient is the beneficial owner. An Approved Issuer Levy of 2% may apply in lieu of NRWT on certain interest paid to non-resident lenders under registered security arrangements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1,000,000 aggregate per category of cross-border related-party transactions per income year. New Zealand does not prescribe mandatory OECD Master File / Local File filings, but contemporaneous OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation is expected when the threshold is exceeded, and Inland Revenue may require disclosure through the IR371 International Questionnaire.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime, but applies the general anti-avoidance rule in the Income Tax Act 2007, OECD BEPS substance requirements, and permanent establishment principles. A tax-exempt International Company must be genuinely managed and controlled outside New Zealand and must maintain real economic substance in its jurisdiction of incorporation, including physical office, qualified staff, and substantive board decision-making. If the entity is a pure letter-box used solely to convert New Zealand advisory fees into exempt foreign income, Inland Revenue may treat the business as having a New Zealand PE or reclassify the company as New Zealand tax-resident.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Understatement of New Zealand-Source Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing FDA 510(k) and CE Mark consulting fees through the International Company while consultants physically perform the services in New Zealand, failing to file IR4 despite carrying on business through a New Zealand PE, deleting cash deposits, or disguising personal remuneration as deductible consulting expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue will reassess the omitted income, charge use-of-money interest, impose a shortfall penalty of 150% of the evaded tax, and prosecute under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Conviction may result in a fine up to NZD 50,000 for a first offence and up to NZD 100,000 for a subsequent offence, in addition to imprisonment for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in evasion may be prosecuted as principals, be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax shortfall under asset recovery powers, be subject to director disqualification for up to five years, and face bail conditions or court-ordered travel bans pending trial. Restraint orders may be made under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company with no physical office, no employed staff, no substantive board meetings, and no independent business purpose while all central management and control is exercised from New Zealand; using the tax-exempt entity solely to avoid 28% New Zealand corporate tax on regulatory advisory fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the entity as a New Zealand tax resident or as having a New Zealand permanent establishment, resulting in full taxation of worldwide income at 28%. Shortfall penalties of 20% for an unacceptable tax position or 100% for an abusive tax position may be imposed, and the International Company registration may be cancelled by the Registrar for failure to maintain qualifying exempt-zone status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structure a sham or engage in artificial tax avoidance can be personally assessed under the Companies Act 1993 for losses caused to creditors, subject to freezing orders, disqualified from managing companies, and prevented from leaving New Zealand where criminal proceedings or asset-recovery applications are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Deficiencies on Bank Wire and Credit Card Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting substantial FDA/CE regulatory consulting fees through bank wires and credit cards without verifying corporate client beneficial ownership, failing to conduct sanctions and PEP screening, splitting payments to avoid detection thresholds, or using third-party payment conduits to obscure the true payee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, civil penalties may reach NZD 2,000,000 for a body corporate and NZD 400,000 for an individual. Money laundering or terrorist financing conduct may be prosecuted under the Crimes Act 1961, carrying imprisonment for up to seven years, asset forfeiture, and confiscation of consulting fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who consents to or knowingly participates in AML/CFT failures is separately liable to civil penalties and criminal prosecution. Courts may impose banning orders preventing the director from managing reporting entities, order restitution of laundered funds, and impose restrictions on international travel pending forfeiture proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Regulatory Representation – FDA 510(k) and CE Mark Compliance Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing conformity certificates, FDA 510(k) clearance statements, or CE Mark certification documentation without a genuine regulatory submission, misrepresenting the International Company as an accredited conformity assessment body, or advising clients that devices are cleared when the technical file is incomplete.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions include enforcement under the New Zealand Fair Trading Act 1986, with fines up to NZD 200,000 for individuals and NZD 600,000 for bodies corporate; FDA civil monetary penalties for false 510(k) submissions under 21 CFR; and penalties for fraudulent CE marking under applicable EU medical device regulation in the destination market. Fraud charges may also be prosecuted under the Crimes Act 1961.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations of conformity or knowingly supervise the issuance of fraudulent certificates face personal criminal liability, consumer-protection disqualification orders, restitution orders to the affected medical device clients, imprisonment, and travel bans where extradition or cross-border investigative proceedings arise.
